questions.prompt: A BJT is biased at \(I_C = 1\ \mathrm{mA}\). Find \(g_m\) in mS (\(V_{th} = kT/q = 26\ \mathrm{mV}\)).
questions.explanation: \(g_m = I_C/V_{th} = 1\ \mathrm{mA}/26\ \mathrm{mV} = 38.5\ \mathrm{mS}\) (reader Eq. 11.24). Unlike a MOSFET, it depends only on current, not size.

options: The resistance of the neutral base region
The base current rising with \(v_{be}\), i.e. the collector's \(g_m\) divided by \(\beta\)
questions.explanation: \(i_b = i_c/\beta = g_mv_{be}/\beta\), so the base looks like a conductance \(g_m/\beta\). Base-width modulation gives \(r_o\).

questions.prompt: At the same bias current, how does a BJT's \(g_m\) compare with a MOSFET's at \(V_{ov} = 0.2\ \mathrm{V}\)?
options: Higher only if the BJT is larger
questions.explanation: Exponential devices give the most transconductance per amp. A MOSFET would need \(V_{ov} = 2V_{th} = 52\ \mathrm{mV}\) to match, outside the square-law region.

questions.prompt: A BJT at \(I_C = 2\ \mathrm{mA}\) sees \(v_{be} = 2\ \mathrm{mV}\). Find the small-signal collector current in µA (ignore \(r_o\)).
questions.explanation: \(i_c = g_mv_{be} = 76.9\ \mathrm{mS}\times2\ \mathrm{mV} = 154\ \mu\mathrm{A}\). Since \(2\ \mathrm{mV} \ll V_{th}\), the linear model is accurate.

questions.prompt: Doubling \(I_C\) changes the hybrid-pi elements how?
questions.explanation: \(g_m = I_C/V_{th}\), \(r_\pi = \beta V_{th}/I_C\), \(r_o = V_A/I_C\). The \(\sqrt2\) law belongs to the MOSFET at fixed size.

questions.prompt: A BJT with \(\beta = 150\) is biased at \(I_C = 0.2\ \mathrm{mA}\) with its emitter grounded. What small-signal resistance (kΩ) is seen looking into the base?
questions.explanation: With the emitter at AC ground the base sees just \(r_\pi = \beta V_{th}/I_C = 19.5\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\). A MOSFET gate would be an open circuit.

questions.prompt: Preview of CS-type gain: a common-emitter stage at \(I_C = 1\ \mathrm{mA}\) has \(R_C = 5\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\) and \(r_o = 100\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\). Find the voltage gain.
questions.explanation: \(A_v = -g_m(R_C\parallel r_o) = -38.5\ \mathrm{mS}\times4.76\ \mathrm{k\Omega} \approx -183\), far more than a comparable MOSFET stage.

questions.prompt: Preview of \(f_T\): what extra capacitance does a forward-active BJT have from base to emitter beyond its junction capacitance?
options: A diffusion capacitance \(g_m\tau_F\) from the minority charge stored in the base
questions.explanation: Raising \(v_{be}\) stores more electrons in the base, \(\Delta Q = \tau_F\Delta I_C\) (reader Eq. 11.31).

questions.prompt: Preview of followers: looking into the emitter of a BJT whose base is driven by an ideal source, what resistance do you see (ignore \(r_o\))?
questions.explanation: The emitter current is \((\beta + 1)i_b\) for a voltage \(v\) across \(r_\pi\), giving \(r_\pi/(\beta + 1) \approx 1/g_m\).
